issues.body: merge_export still increments unkeyed and drops fresh records whose id is absent, while fresh_by_id[rid] still overwrites earlier records with the same ID. Thus an ID-less record can disappear and an arbitrary duplicate can win before the board is published. This contradicts the documented fail-closed safety posture for corrupt exports, and the new self-test/end-to-end test still exercises only malformed JSON rather than invalid record identity.
issues.fix_hint: Validate record identity before merging: require each fresh record to have a non-empty string ID and reject duplicate IDs with a nonzero exit; preferably validate duplicates and IDs in the committed input too, or narrowly document and test any necessary committed-input grandfathering. Add pure and end-to-end refusal tests proving that neither ID-less nor duplicate-ID exports push a branch.
issues.title: Malformed record identities are still silently normalized

issues.body: emit_json still inserts BRANCH and the gh-derived PR value directly between JSON quotes. Quotes, backslashes, or control characters in either value produce invalid JSON, so --json does not reliably satisfy its documented scheduler contract.
issues.fix_hint: Construct the entire result with a JSON encoder such as the already-required python3, passing values as arguments or environment data rather than interpolating JSON text. Add a test that parses output for a branch containing JSON-significant characters.
issues.title: Machine-readable output is still not JSON-escaped

verdict.summary: Round 2 is stagnant: both prior findings remain materially unchanged. The merge still silently drops fresh records without IDs and collapses duplicate IDs with last-record-wins semantics, despite documenting fail-closed behavior for corrupt exports. The JSON output still interpolates branch and PR strings without JSON escaping. The added tests cover neither malformed record identity nor JSON-significant output values, so the source-of-record publication path remains unsafe for structurally corrupt exports and its machine-readable contract remains unreliable.
